steps.title: What is Splendor?
steps.content: You are a Renaissance merchant acquiring gem mines, transportation, and shops to earn the most **prestige points**. Collect gems, buy development cards that give you permanent purchasing power, and attract visits from nobles. The first player to reach **15 prestige points** triggers the final round!

steps.title: What's on the Table
steps.content:
Let's look at the components:

- **Gem tokens** (40 total) - 7 each of 5 colors: Diamond (white), Sapphire (blue), Emerald (green), Ruby (red), Onyx (black)
- **Gold tokens** (5) - Wildcards, only obtained by reserving cards
- **Development cards** (90) in 3 tiers:
  - Level 1 (green dots) - Cheap, low/no prestige
  - Level 2 (yellow dots) - Mid-cost, some prestige
  - Level 3 (blue dots) - Expensive, high prestige
- **Noble tiles** - Worth 3 prestige each; they visit you automatically

Each development card shows a **gem cost** (bottom-left), a **gem bonus** (top-right corner), and possibly **prestige points** (top-left).

steps.title: Setting Up the Game
steps.content:
1. Place gem tokens in the center based on player count:
   - **2 players**: 4 of each gem color
   - **3 players**: 5 of each gem color
   - **4 players**: 7 of each gem color
   - Always use all 5 gold tokens
2. Shuffle each tier of development cards separately
3. Place each deck face-down, then reveal **4 cards** face-up from each tier (3 rows of 4)
4. Reveal **noble tiles** equal to players + 1 (e.g., 4 nobles for 3 players)
5. Youngest player goes first

steps.title: What You Do on Your Turn
steps.content:
On your turn, you must perform **exactly one** of these four actions:

**1. Take 3 different gems** - Pick 1 token each of 3 different colors.

**2. Take 2 same-color gems** - Pick 2 tokens of one color, but only if there are **4 or more** of that color available.

**3. Reserve a card** - Take any face-up card (or the top of a deck) into your hand and receive 1 **gold wildcard token**. You can hold at most 3 reserved cards.

**4. Purchase a card** - Buy a face-up card or one you previously reserved by paying its gem cost.

**Important:** You can never have more than **10 tokens** at the end of your turn. Return extras to the supply.

steps.title: Buying Cards & Gem Bonuses
steps.content:
When you **purchase a card**, pay its gem cost using your tokens. But here's the key mechanic:

**Each card you own gives a permanent gem bonus.** This bonus counts as a gem of that color for all future purchases. For example:
- A card costs 3 blue + 2 red
- You own 2 cards with blue bonuses
- You only need to pay 1 blue token + 2 red tokens!

Gold tokens are **wildcards** and can substitute for any gem color.

Purchased cards stay in front of you — their bonuses stack and never go away. This is the engine-building core of the game!

steps.title: Noble Visits
steps.content:
Nobles visit you **automatically** at the end of your turn if you meet their requirements. Each noble tile shows the gem bonuses needed (from your purchased cards, not tokens).

For example, a noble might require 3 blue + 3 red gem bonuses. Once you have that many cards of those colors, the noble visits you and you take the tile — worth **3 prestige points**.

**Key rules:**
- You don't spend anything — nobles just check your card collection
- If you qualify for multiple nobles on the same turn, you pick one
- Noble tiles cannot be reserved

steps.title: Strategy Tips
steps.content:
A few tips for your first game:

- **Focus on Level 1 cards early** — they're cheap and build your engine
- **Look at the nobles** — plan your purchases to attract them for 3 bonus points
- **Don't hoard tokens** — spend them on cards to get permanent bonuses
- **Reserve strategically** — block opponents from key cards or save expensive ones for later
- **Watch opponents** — if someone is close to a card you need, reserve it or buy it first

steps.title: Let's Play a Practice Round
steps.content:
Let's walk through some sample turns:

**Turn 1:** Take 3 different gem tokens — say 1 blue, 1 red, and 1 green. Now you have tokens to spend.

**Turn 2:** Look at the Level 1 cards. You see one that costs 1 blue + 1 red + 1 green and gives a white gem bonus. Buy it! Pay your 3 tokens. Now you have a permanent white discount.

**Turn 3:** Take 2 tokens of the same color (e.g., 2 black) since there are 4+ available.

**Turn 4:** A Level 2 card costs 2 white + 3 black. Your white card bonus covers 1 white, so you only need 1 white token + 3 black tokens. Build that engine!

Keep buying cards to build your bonuses. The first player to reach **15 prestige points** triggers the final round — finish the round so everyone has equal turns, then the highest score wins!
